# CGRX v0.1.0-alpha.11

This alpha focuses on faster project-wide analysis, refactoring discovery, and a more useful graph explorer while preserving fail-closed evidence semantics.

- Adds a React/TypeScript/Three.js project graph explorer with deterministic clustered layout, package grouping, stable camera state, and read-only evidence overlays.
- Adds background similarity indexing for exact duplicates, near-duplicates, structurally similar code, and shared proven functionality to speed up refactoring discovery.
- Adds snapshot-local query indexes for symbols, documents, proven arcs, and adjacency so orient, search, trace, usages, snippets, architecture, risks, and refactor queries reuse the same bounded generation-local structures.
- Adds generation-bound background rebuilds and honest partial-index telemetry so stale workers cannot publish into newer snapshots.
- Adds prepared-orient reuse and an `orient` benchmark path to reduce repeated warm-query work while retaining semantic-reranker freshness when Laya is enabled.
- Speeds up architecture and risk queries with snapshot-local caches and reusable lookup indexes while keeping coverage gaps and ambiguous identities fail-closed.
- Speeds up dirty-worktree refresh by using bounded Git status options and preserving both sides of staged renames without weakening HEAD-change checks.
- Keeps exact duplicates separate from heuristic similarity and preserves proof hashes, snapshot identity, dynamic-dispatch uncertainty, and coverage-gap blockers throughout refactor suggestions.
- Rebuilds the embedded web bundle reproducibly from TypeScript sources and adds typechecked Three.js dependencies and license metadata.

The downloadable Apple Silicon archive is accompanied by `SHA256SUMS`. Linux and Intel macOS remain pinned source-install paths with Rust 1.89.0.
